children: NVIDIA’s board accepted CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, citing a lack of candor about his personal conduct and violations of company standards, Chairman Harvey Jones said at a November 18 meeting.
California is investigating whether NVIDIA chips or confidential data reached China and whether the company misled investors about related risks. No wrongdoing has been found.
NVIDIA shares fell 3.3% to $145.98 on Nov. 19, on nearly twice normal volume, then dropped 2.74% in Friday premarket to a 52-week low of $141.97 amid CEO transition uncertainty.
NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA)’s Vera Rubin platform reportedly generated about $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, compared with $11 billion for Blackwell in its first quarter.
NVIDIA reported $390 billion in supply commitments in fiscal Q3 2027, up from $119 billion two quarters earlier. Its cloud-industry backlog rose to $2.5 trillion from $2 trillion in three months.

NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) reported strong earnings and raised its revenue outlook for next year, while its shares continued to fall. Investors expressed concerns about the sustainability of AI demand.
NVIDIA beat estimates and forecast $130 billion in revenue, but shares fell amid tighter U.S. export rules. The firm halted H200 shipments to China and excluded the market from its revenue outlook.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent gave NVIDIA (NVDA) 10 days to answer questions on whether it knowingly sold chips to China to boost earnings.
Investor Mark Kistenmacher filed a proposed shareholder class action against NVIDIA and Jensen Huang, alleging misleading disclosures about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang and related risks.
The U.S. Justice Department is reviewing NVIDIA’s proposed $12.9 billion Hugging Face acquisition as part of a broader antitrust probe into the chipmaker’s deals and business practices.
